newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso stands by central bank over forex.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso stands by central bank over forex.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso supports the central bank's foreign exchange policy and has rejected criticisms reportedly made by a senior member of his cabinet, a presidential spokesman said Tuesday.
"The foreign exchange policy is a matter for the government, and the president has every confidence in the policies that the central bank is taking," Cardoso's spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters.

With Brazilian stocks already tumbling amid profit-taking and concerns over recent devaluations in Asia, the financial markets turned even more unsettled Tuesday afternoon after reports that Communications Minister Sergio Motta had criticized the central bank.

Motta, a friend of Cardoso known for his aggressive style of politics, was quoted by news wires as casting aspersions on Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco, who effectively runs exchange rate policy.

"There's no point carrying out stabilization of the economy without having an (economic) development plan. The Asian currency crisis shows us that Gustavo Franco is wrong," Motta was quoted by local agency Agencia O Globo as saying.
"The president does not believe the minister made that declaration, and if he did, he was wrong," the spokesman said.
He also said Tuesday's 8.5 percent plunge on the Sao Paulo stock exchange reflected profit-taking and did not represent the beginning of a run on Brazilian investments.
"There is no reason for an attack on the real (currency) in Brazil," Amaral said "The economic team and the president are calm."
